questions.question:
**Directions: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The invited guests preferred orange juice than hot coffee or chilled grapes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'than hot coffee'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the preposition 'than' is incorrect.
 
• From the given sentence, the word **'Prefer'** is **usually followed by 'to' and not 'than'** because the word itself means **'like something or someone more than another'**.
 
• '**To**' here **refers to the relationship between orange juice and hot coffee or chilled grapes**.
 
• Also, we use **prefer "than"** when **the comparison is between infinitives to infinitives **( infinitives are **to+ first form of the verb**).
 
• We use **prefer "to"** when the **comparison is between noun to noun** and **gerund to gerund** ( gerund is **V+ing form of the verb**).
 
• Therefore, the **preposition 'to'** should be used **in place of** the **preposition 'than'**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2**.

Correct Sentence__: *The invited guests preferred orange juice **to hot coffee** or chilled grapes*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

__As many as__ I care for her, I still have to disagree with her on this topic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'As much as'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the underlined segment, the **adjective 'many'** is **incorrect**.
 
• The **adjective 'many'** means **a large number**. We use "**as many as**" for **countable nouns**.
 
• The **adjective 'much'** means **a great amount or quantity**. We use "**as much as**" for **uncountable nouns**.
 
• Therefore, the **adjective 'much'** should be used **in place of** the **adjective 'many'**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**The Correct Sentence is:** ***As much as** I care for her, I still have to disagree with her on this topic*.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The coach received the members of the team with great excitement.

options.text: The members of the team had been received by the coach with great excitement.
The members of the team was received by the coach with great excitement.
The members of the team could be received by the coach with great excitement.
The members of the team were received by the coach with great excitement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The members of the team were received by the coach with great excitement**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and 'The coach' is the subject and '**the members of the team**' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'The coach' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'the members of the team' becomes the subject.
 
• The passive format "'were + V3 (received)" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4*.*

**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Anush was very afraid of stray dogs.

B. Anush’s mother saw the dog chasing her son.

C. One evening, when a street dog barked at him, Anush turned and started running.

D. The dog ran after him barking loudly and fiercely.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ACDB'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence 'A' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about the noun "Anush". Hence, 'A' is the first part.
 
• The "street dog" mentioned in the sentence 'C' refers back to the 'stray dogs' mentioned in the sentence 'A'. Hence, 'C' follows 'A'.
 
• The pronoun "him" mentioned in the sentence 'D' refers back to the noun "Anush" mentioned in the sentence 'C'. Hence, 'D' follows 'C'.
 
• The sentence 'B' is the concluding sentence. Hence, 'B' is the last sentence.

 

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *Anush was very afraid of stray dogs. One evening, when a street dog barked at him, Anush turned and started running. The dog ran after him barking loudly and fiercely. Anush’s mother saw the dog chasing her son.*

• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The traveler inquired, "Will there be a shelter for strangers?”

options.text: The traveler inquired if would there be a shelter for strangers.
The traveler inquired if there will be a shelter for strangers.
The traveler inquired if there would be a shelter for strangers.
The traveler inquired whether will there be a shelter for strangers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The traveler inquired if there would be a shelter for strangers'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or ____converting direct speech into indirect speech__:​
 __
 
• The commas and inverted commas are removed and the 'question mark' is replaced by 'full stop' and '**if**' is **included**.
 
• The present simple tense format 'Subject + V1 (will) + Object' will be changed into the past simple tense format 'Subject + V2 (would) + Object'.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:-
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object)
 Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
 
 

 Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)

• Given Idiom: ***Every cloud has a silver lining*** means **there is something good in everything that’s bad**.

• From the given options, the second option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Directions: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Everyone are very well equipped with his own weapons.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Everyone are'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the plural form of the verb 'are' is incorrect.
 
• We know that a singular 'subject' will always take a singular 'verb'.
 
• The singular subject 'Everyone' will take the singular verb 'ís'.
 
• Therefore, the singular verb 'is' should be used in place of the plural verb 'are'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence__: *Everyone is very well equipped with his own weapons*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• *Subjects and verbs must agree with one another in number (singular or plural).*
 
• *Thus, if a subject is singular, its verb must also be singular; if a subject is plural, its verb must also be plural*.
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में, verb के plural रूप 'are' का उपयोग सही नहीं है।
 
• हम जानते हैं कि एक singular 'subject' हमेशा एक singular verb लेगा ।
 
• Singular subject 'everyone' singular verb 'ís' लेगा ।
 
• इसलिए, singular verb 'is' का उपयोग plural verb के स्थान पर किया जाना चाहिए।

इसलिए, सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है ।

सही वाक्य__: *Everyone is very well equipped with his own weapons.*
